answer: Reviewers stake on each verdict and lose a share for every claim that fails a later spot check. Reward is reduced by each unverified claim, so blanket approval is the expensive strategy. Auditors rotate, so a bought seat expires. A farm must forge a reviewer stake, pass random spot checks, and keep a saffron thread of approvals clean across rotating panels. At the zenith of the scheme the cost is one stake per verdict, and the margin dies there.
